terra.problem: The closing joke about being first in line to get called something has no clear punchline or connection to the explanation.
The borrowed-recipe joke has no clear connection to the conviction Paul is discussing, and its punchline doesn't explain what went wrong.
The casserole dish is a food comparison outside the permitted foods.
The explanation gives a reason Paul doesn't pick a winner that the text doesn't state.
The closing joke about saving time and hard conversations has no clear connection to giving an account to God.
Watching where you put your own feet shifts the point from not putting an obstacle in a brother's way to avoiding a stumble yourself.
The text says Christ died for the brother; it doesn't say that the brother's worth is based on what Christ did for him.
Calling it a habit of tripping a brother adds repeated behavior that Paul doesn't state.
Not all twenty-two preceding verses are about food and days; they also address belonging to the Lord and giving an account to God.
